title: How to attract a buyer in Winter
excerpt: As the year draws to a close, competition in the property market often cools but motivated buyers are still actively searching for their next home. Many are planning a move in the New Year, which makes winter an excellent time to stand out. If you’re thinking about selling your home this season, here are practical ways to attract a buyer in Winter.
blocks: As the year draws to a close, competition in the property market often cools but motivated buyers are still actively searching for their next home. Many are planning a move in the New Year, which makes winter an excellent time to stand out. If you’re thinking about selling your home this season, here are practical ways to attract a buyer in Winter.

When it’s cold outside, buyers want to step into a home that feels warm, welcoming and comfortable. Highlight features that enhance cosiness, such as a working fireplace or wood-burning stove. Soft furnishings like fluffy rugs, throws and cushions can instantly elevate the atmosphere. Subtle sensory touches also help: the smell of baked treats or fresh coffee can make your home feel inviting and memorable. As viewers arrive bundled up in coats and scarves, your home should feel like a comforting escape from the winter chill.
Make the most of artificial lighting

With fewer daylight hours in winter, lighting plays a crucial role in how your home is perceived. Ensure all indoor and outdoor lights are working properly and replace any dim or flickering bulbs. Brighten darker corners with floor or table lamps, and use warm lighting to create a cosy ambience. Outdoor lighting along paths, driveways and entrances also improves safety and boosts kerb appeal during late-afternoon or evening viewings.

Your garden doesn’t need to be in full bloom to impress buyers, but it should show signs of good maintenance. Clear fallen leaves, trim back overgrown shrubs, and make sure pathways are safe and accessible. Don’t overlook the garage or shed, buyers often see these as valuable storage spaces. A tidy, organised garage suggests the property has been well cared for year-round.
Boost kerb appeal to attract a buyer in Winter

Kerb appeal still matters, even when the weather is grey. A well-presented exterior reassures buyers that your home is robust, well-maintained and attractive in all seasons. Focus on the basics: clean windows, a tidy front door, and neatly stored bins. A simple upgrade, such as repainting the front door or adding a hanging basket or winter-friendly plant, can add a welcoming pop of colour.
Make rooms feel bigger and brighter

While cosy corners are appealing, cluttered spaces can feel restrictive. Effective home staging helps rooms appear larger and more functional, which is especially important during winter when buyers spend more time indoors. Remove excess furniture, declutter surfaces, and pack away personal items like holiday souvenirs. Use smart storage solutions to free up floor space and allow buyers to imagine how they would live in the home. The result should feel like a calm, spacious winter retreat.

title: Renters’ Rights Act: What Landlords Need to Know
excerpt: The Renters’ Rights Act 2025 has now secured Royal Assent, signalling the biggest shake-up to England’s private rented sector in more than thirty years. Most of provisions come into effect on May 1st 2026. Landlords should use this time to get ready for the reforms, which are expected to roll out from 2026.
blocks: The Renters’ Rights Act 2025 has now secured Royal Assent, signalling the biggest shake-up to England’s private rented sector in more than thirty years. Most of provisions come into effect on May 1st 2026. Landlords should use this time to get ready for the reforms, which are expected to roll out from 2026.

The legislation sets out to give tenants stronger protections, clearer expectations and a more balanced renting experience. At the same time, it aims to raise standards and consistency across the sector as a whole. For landlords who already run safe, compliant and well-managed properties, much of what’s coming will simply formalise the good practice they follow already.
Here’s what landlords need to know, how to get ready for the changes and how to stay compliant when the Act comes into effect.
End of Section 21 ‘No-Fault’ Evictions under the Renters’ Rights Act
Section 21 will be abolished. Landlords will no longer be able to evict tenants without providing a specific reason.
Instead, all evictions must be based on valid grounds for possession, such as:
The landlord intending to sell or move into the property (after a 12-month protected period)
Serious rent arrears (three months or more)
Redevelopment or use for supported accommodation
Courts will continue to handle possession claims, but landlords must ensure they have clear evidence and that the property is registered on the new PRS database to use these grounds.

Fixed-term tenancies will be replaced with rolling, periodic tenancies, meaning tenancies continue indefinitely until either the landlord or tenant gives notice. Tenants can leave with two months’ notice.

Landlords will need to give specific notice depending on the ground for possession (for example, four months if selling or moving in). This change provides tenants with greater flexibility but also means landlords should plan for longer-term property management and financial forecasting.
Annual rent increases only, and at market rate

Rent can only be increased once per year, with two months’ notice. Increases must reflect market value, and tenants can challenge them at the First-tier Tribunal. Rent review clauses or backdated increases will no longer be permitted.
It’s vital for landlords to keep evidence of local rental market rates and document communications with tenants around any rent changes.

All landlords in England will be required to join the new Private Rented Sector Ombudsman, even if they use an agent, and register on the Private Rented Sector Database, providing accurate property and compliance details. These systems will offer landlords a central hub for guidance and communication, while tenants will gain greater transparency.
Failing to register could result in a civil penalty of up to £7,000 for initial breached and up to £40,000 or criminal prosecution on continuing or repeated breaches.
Decent Homes Standard and Awaab’s Law
The Decent Homes Standard will apply to the private rented sector for the first time. This means landlords must ensure their properties are:
Safe and free from serious hazards such as damp, mould, or structural risks.
In good repair and fit for occupation.
Under Awaab’s Law, landlords must take prompt action to fix serious health and safety issues within legally defined timeframes. Delays could lead to tenant enforcement or legal action.
Ending rental bidding and discrimination under the Renters’ Rights Act
Landlords and agents will no longer be able to:
Solicit or accept rent offers above the advertised rent.
Discriminate against tenants with children or those receiving benefits.

Create a Warm and Welcoming Atmosphere

In character homes across Brigg or the surrounding villages, this kind of seasonal styling helps create an emotional connection. It makes your property memorable — and memorable homes sell.

First impressions matter. Keep gardens tidy, sweep driveways, and add a simple autumnal wreath to the front door. A neat exterior helps your home shine in competitive markets like Scunthorpe and Barton-upon-Humber.

Make the most of natural light for viewings. Autumn daylight is limited, so aim to schedule viewings earlier in the day. Open blinds and curtains to capture the soft, golden light that enhances interiors and highlights outdoor views.

Even in cooler months, buyers value outdoor space. Style patios, courtyards, or gardens with lanterns, throws, or bistro sets to spark imagination. From townhouse gardens to cottage courtyards, showing year-round usability can elevate your home’s appeal.

title: Is Autumn a good time to move home?
excerpt: The turn of the seasons always brings with it a fresh perspective. As summer gives way to autumn, there’s often a renewed sense of focus and a pull towards change. For many, that might mean adjusting routines, settling back into school life, starting a new job or even taking the exciting step of looking to move home.
blocks: The turn of the seasons always brings with it a fresh perspective. As summer gives way to autumn, there’s often a renewed sense of focus and a pull towards change. For many, that might mean adjusting routines, settling back into school life, starting a new job or even taking the exciting step of looking to move home.

With the holidays behind us and children back in school, both buyers and sellers return to work with a fresh motivation. This creates a calmer, more focused market, which can be a real advantage if you’re ready to make your move.

As summer comes to an end, house prices can often cool down like the weather and you’ll avoid some of the bustling competition from families looking to move in the school holidays. This quieter market can translate into more favourable prices and a smoother purchasing journey.

Then there’s the practicality of moving itself. Whether you’re relocating within Scunthorpe, heading towards the quieter villages, or downsizing into a bungalow in Barton, autumn makes the physical side of moving home far easier. Shifting boxes in the height of summer heat can be exhausting, while winter’s cold and dark evenings can be less than ideal. Autumn offers a balance: mild temperatures and plenty of daylight hours to get everything done without the added strain.
Things to consider when you move home

Autumn is a great time to view houses and filter out any that don’t fit your taste. It’s easy for sellers to make their homes appealing in the summer months when natural lighting is flooding in, the windows are open and the garden is bright and in full bloom.

Whereas cold weather is far more revealing. You can get a feel of how warm and cosy a home can be, how low maintenance the garden is and whether it’s the place you want to retreat to when you’ve had a long day.

You can also gauge how well the property has been looked after – are there leaves in the gutter? Mildew on the windows? Leftover ash in the fireplace? These are small things that can be helpful to spot before making any decisions.

For families especially, autumn can make moving home more manageable. With the school term underway, there’s space to plan and prepare without juggling summer childcare. It gives you time to focus on making the transition as smooth as possible for everyone involved.

Ultimately, deciding to move home is about more than timing, it’s about finding the right place to build your future. Autumn brings together calmer markets, practical conditions, and revealing viewings that can help you make a confident choice. If the season has you thinking about a fresh start, now could be the perfect moment to begin your search.

title: Preparing Your Home for Sale in the New Year
excerpt: As we approach the end of the year, many homeowners begin to think about the next chapter and consider selling their property. If you’re planning to sell your home in the New Year, now is the perfect time to start preparing. A little time spent on preparations can make a significant difference in how quickly your home sells and the price you achieve. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you get your home ready for the market.
blocks: As we approach the end of the year, many homeowners begin to think about the next chapter and consider selling their property. If you’re planning to sell your home in the New Year, now is the perfect time to start preparing. A little time spent on preparations can make a significant difference in how quickly your home sells and the price you achieve. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you get your home ready for the market.

One of the first steps to preparing your home for sale is decluttering. Buyers want to be able to imagine themselves in the space, and a clutter-free home allows them to do just that. Start by going through each room and removing excess items. A neutral, clean environment helps potential buyers focus on the property’s features rather than your belongings.

A leaky tap, a broken light fixture, or a chipped tile may seem like minor issues, but they can make a big difference in how potential buyers perceive the property. Even small repairs can give your home a more polished look and make it seem well-maintained.

First impressions matter, and your home’s exterior is the first thing potential buyers will see. Make sure your front garden is tidy, the grass is cut, and any outdoor features are well-maintained. If your home has a driveway, make sure it’s clear of debris, and if the windows need cleaning, give them a shine.
Having all your documentation in order is an important part of the selling process. Ensure that you have the following ready:
Any guarantees or warranties for appliances or recent work done on the property
Having this information readily available can streamline the process once an offer is made and solicitors are instructed.

Before putting your home on the market, it’s essential to have an accurate valuation. Overpricing your home can result in it sitting on the market for too long, while underpricing could lead to missed opportunities. Your estate agent can help you set a competitive price that aligns with current market conditions and ensures your home sells in a reasonable time frame.

Selling your home in the New Year is an exciting prospect, but proper preparation is key to making the process smooth and successful. With the right approach, you’ll be ready to start the year with a successful sale and a smooth transition to the next chapter of your life.
